results.title: Pharmacovigilance in Cell and Gene Therapy: Evolving Challenges in Risk Management and Long-Term Follow-Up | Drug Safety | Springer Nature Link
results.content: This review highlights several distinctive advances, including a CRO-based framework for real-time, AI-enhanced pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) and safety-monitoring dashboards; a comprehensive pediatric transition-of-care roadmap aligning developmental milestones with long-term follow-up (LTFU); and a comparative evaluation of global LTFU frameworks extending beyond the USA and EU, alongside broader insights into predictive analytics, registry integration, and ethical considerations shaping the future of PVG in CGTs. Given the risks associated with CAR T-cell and gene therapies, long-term safety surveillance is essential to maintain a favorable benefit–risk profile and preserve the curative potential of these advanced treatments [88, 93]. Cardiovascular toxicity has emerged as a critical long-term safety concern across multiple CGT platforms, including CAR T-cell therapies, AAV-based gene therapies, and CRISPR-mediated interventions [95]. In Japan, post-marketing all-case surveillance (PACS) remains compulsory for every approved CGT, mandating the collection of comprehensive safety and efficacy data from all treated patients, including registry enrollment and re-examination periods to monitor long-term outcomes [138:108–16."), 139, P.a.M.D.A. risk management plan and postmarketing surveillance in Japan. Early real-world cohorts have begun to reveal safety signals that diverge from controlled trial observations, such as delayed or atypical CRS presentations in frail, pediatric, or autoimmune patient populations treated with CAR T-cell therapies outside traditional oncology indications [144:17.")]. For example, pediatric patients who receive CAR T-cells or gene therapy for congenital disorders should undergo periodic neurodevelopmental assessments and endocrine reviews (thyroid function, pubertal development, etc.), since cases of growth delay and hypothyroidism have been noted after intensive treatments [165,166:77–83."),167. International pediatric PVG networks and data-sharing initiatives are increasingly pivotal in monitoring long-term outcomes of CGTs. By aggregating global pediatric data, these collaborative efforts facilitate the detection of delayed or rare AEs, thereby enhancing the safety profiles of emerging therapies across various indications. AI and machine learning (ML) approaches must be specifically tailored to the biological complexity of CGTs. Designing these algorithms requires the ability to detect clonal hematopoiesis in patients receiving integration-based therapies, identify CRISPR-associated off-target edits and indel patterns, monitor immune recovery after CAR T-cells or AAV administration, and distinguish overlapping syndromes, such as differentiating ICANS from stroke or CRS from HLH, particularly in pediatric populations where clinical signs may be subtle or atypical [33:3978–92.")]. *et al.* Pharmacovigilance in Cell and Gene Therapy: Evolving Challenges in Risk Management and Long-Term Follow-Up.

Title: CBD Safety in Long-Term Pediatric Treatments | Get Med Card
# CBD Safety in Long-Term Pediatric Treatments. Parents, pediatricians, and researchers alike are asking the big question: is CBD safe for long-term pediatric treatments? That distinction has opened the door to exploring CBD as a therapeutic option for children struggling with conditions like epilepsy, autism spectrum disorders, anxiety, and chronic pain. This article digs into the nuances of CBD safety in long-term pediatric use. * CBD shows therapeutic promise for pediatric conditions such as epilepsy, anxiety, and autism. * Long-term safety data is limited, but short- to medium-term studies suggest CBD is generally well-tolerated. ## **Understanding CBD in Pediatrics**. ### **What Makes Pediatric CBD Use Unique?**. Parents often seek CBD as an alternative when conventional medications don’t work or cause intolerable side effects. ## **The Benefits of CBD in Pediatric Care**. The key takeaway here is that when CBD is properly dosed and monitored, it can provide life-changing benefits for children whose seizures were previously uncontrollable. ## **Potential Risks of Long-Term CBD Use in Children**. One of the most consistent safety concerns with CBD is its effect on liver enzymes. In some children, especially those taking other medications, long-term CBD use can elevate liver function markers. CBD is metabolized in the liver using the same enzymes as many common medications. In children who may already be on complex medication regimens, CBD can amplify or reduce drug effects, potentially leading to dangerous outcomes. The big unknown with long-term pediatric CBD is its effect on brain development. Parents considering long-term CBD should commit to ongoing monitoring. Some states allow medical CBD use for children under specific conditions, while others restrict access. CBD holds undeniable promise in pediatric medicine, especially for children with treatment-resistant conditions like epilepsy. By choosing high-quality products, working closely with a knowledgeable pediatrician, and committing to long-term monitoring, families can explore CBD as a potential tool without compromising safety. ### Is CBD safe for children to take long-term? Current research suggests CBD is generally well-tolerated in children, especially for conditions like epilepsy. CBD does interact with brain receptors, but the long-term effects on cognition and development are not fully understood. This is one of the main reasons more research is urgently needed before CBD can be widely recommended for pediatric use.

results.title: Long-term endocrine disorders in children born from pregnancies conceived following fertility treatments - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Long-term endocrine disorders in children born from pregnancies conceived following fertility treatments. Fertility treatments do not appear to increase the risk for long-term endocrine disorders. Despite the endocrine basis of several infertility etiologies, data on long-term endocrine consequences in offspring conceived following fertility treatments remain limited. ### Aim. To determine the risk of long-term endocrine disorders among children born after in-vitro fertilization (IVF) and ovulation induction (OI) as compared with spontaneous pregnancies. Hospitalization rates up to the age of 18 years involving endocrine disorders were compared between children delivered following pregnancies achieved by IVF, OI, and spontaneous pregnancies. Hospitalizations up to the age of 18 years involving endocrine disorders were comparable in children delivered following IVF (0.4%), OI (0.8%) and spontaneous pregnancies (0.5%; *p* = 0.09). Using the Cox regression model while controlling for confounders, no significant association was noted between IVF (adjusted HR = 0.95, CI 0.51–1.87), or OI (adjusted HR = 1.32, CI 0.78–2.24) conceived pregnancies, and long-term pediatric endocrine morbidity. Singletons conceived via fertility treatment do not appear to be at an increased risk for long-term endocrine disorders. Recently, several studies found higher rates of long-term morbidity in offspring conceived following fertility treatments, including infectious [10], neurological [11], gastrointestinal [12], respiratory, obstructive sleep apnea [13], oncological [14], and dermatological morbidities [15]. Nevertheless, despite the endocrine basis of several infertility etiologies in couples undergoing fertility treatments, data on long-term endocrine health consequences in the offspring remains limited. The current study was aimed to examine whether fertility treatments including OI and IVF are associated with the long-term incidence of endocrine disorders among offspring up to the age of 18 years. In this large population-based study, singletons conceived following fertility treatment did not appear to be at an increased risk for long-term endocrine disorders. In recent years, a growing body of evidence suggests that children conceived through the use of fertility treatments are at an increased risk of long-term perinatal morbidity. ### Fertility treatments and offspring pediatric infectious morbidities: results of a population-based cohort with a median follow-up of 10 years. ### Fertility treatments and pediatric neoplasms of the offspring: results of a population-based cohort with a median follow-up of 10 years. ### Long-term cardiovascular morbidity in children born following fertility treatment.
